questions.knowledge_point: Computing One Iteration of the Newton-Raphson Method
questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,2]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)={x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2xy+3{y}^{2}+x.
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[1,\,0]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

| ${x}_{1}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2xy+3{y}^{2}+x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2xy+3{y}^{2}+x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2xy-4x-2y+1 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+6y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy-4x-2y+1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-2x+6y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy-4x-2y+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-2x+6y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2y-4 & 2x-2 \\ 2x-2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2y-4 & 2x-2 \\ 2x-2 & 6\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2xy-4x-2y+1 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+6y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with
${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}2y-4 & 2x-2 \\ 2x-2 & 6\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2xy-4x-2y+1 \\ {x}^{2}-2x+6y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(0)-4 & 2(1)-2 \\ 2(1)-2 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2(1)(0)-4(1)-2(0)+1 \\ (1)^{2}-2(1)+6(0)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-4)\cdot 6-(0)\cdot (0)}[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{24}[\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.25 \\ 0.167\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=3{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+x.
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T}.$

| $[$ | $2$ | {{field-1}} | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | $-3$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} | $-4$ | {{field-3}} |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6xy-4x+1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy-4x+1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-4y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(6xy-4x+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-4y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6y-4 & 6x \\ 6x & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6y-4 & 6x \\ 6x & -4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}6xy-4x+1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6y-4 & 6x \\ 6x & -4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}6xy-4x+1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6(1)-4 & 6(1) \\ 6(1) & -4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}6(1)(1)-4(1)+1 \\ 3(1)^{2}-4(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 6 & -4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Two Iterations of the Newton-Raphson Method
questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-1,1]\times [-1,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=7{x}^{2}y-2xy+3{y}^{3}-1.
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-1,\,0]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to **three decimal places.**

| ${x}_{2}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(7{x}^{2}y-2xy+3{y}^{3}-1) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(7{x}^{2}y-2xy+3{y}^{3}-1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14xy-2y \\ 7{x}^{2}-2x+9{y}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(14xy-2y) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(7{x}^{2}-2x+9{y}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(14xy-2y) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(7{x}^{2}-2x+9{y}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}14y & 14x-2 \\ 14x-2 & 18y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}14y & 14x-2 \\ 14x-2 & 18y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}14xy-2y \\ 7{x}^{2}-2x+9{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}14y & 14x-2 \\ 14x-2 & 18y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}14xy-2y \\ 7{x}^{2}-2x+9{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}14(0) & 14(-1)-2 \\ 14(-1)-2 & 18(0)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}14(-1)(0)-2(0) \\ 7(-1)^{2}-2(-1)+9(0)^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}0 & -16 \\ -16 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{0\cdot 0-(-16)\cdot (-16)}[\begin{aligned}0 & 16 \\ 16 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{256}[\begin{aligned}144 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-0.438 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=4{x}^{2}y-3x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}-2x.
$$

Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T},$ and compute the components of the first iteration. Round the answer for ${x}_{1}$ to **three decimal places**.

| $[$ | {{field-1}} | $2$ | $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ | $-5$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | {{field-2}} | {{field-3}} |  |  |  |

| ${x}_{1}≈[$ | $0.594$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-4}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}y-3x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}-2x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}y-3x{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}-2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(4{x}^{2}-6xy) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(4{x}^{2}-6xy)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x-6y \\ 8x-6y & -6x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x-6y \\ 8x-6y & -6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}8y+2 & 8x-6y \\ 8x-6y & -6x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}8xy-3{y}^{2}+2x-2 \\ 4{x}^{2}-6xy\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}8(1)+2 & 8(1)-6(1) \\ 8(1)-6(1) & -6(1)\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}8(1)(1)-3(1)^{2}+2(1)-2 \\ 4(1)^{2}-6(1)(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}10 & 2 \\ 2 & -6\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-13/32 \\ -15/32\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{13}{32} \\ -\frac{15}{32}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{13}{32} \\ -\frac{15}{32}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.594 \\ 0.531\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Two Iterations of the Newton-Raphson Method
questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-1,2]\times [-2,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=2x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y+3{x}^{2}.
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[2,\,-2]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[1.75,\,0.125]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{2}≈[$ | $-0.301$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-1}} |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y+3{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}y+3{x}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-2xy+6x \\ 4xy-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{y}^{2}-2xy+6x) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy-{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(2{y}^{2}-2xy+6x) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(4xy-{x}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2y+6 & 4y-2x \\ 4y-2x & 4x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}-2y+6 & 4y-2x \\ 4y-2x & 4x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-2xy+6x \\ 4xy-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}-2y+6 & 4y-2x \\ 4y-2x & 4x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-2xy+6x \\ 4xy-{x}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.75 \\ 0.125\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-2(0.125)+6 & 4(0.125)-2(1.75) \\ 4(0.125)-2(1.75) & 4(1.75)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2(0.125)^{2}-2(1.75)(0.125)+6(1.75) \\ 4(1.75)(0.125)-(1.75)^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.75 \\ 0.125\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}5.75 & -3 \\ -3 & 7\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}10.093\,75 \\ -2.187\,5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.75 \\ 0.125\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(5.75)\cdot 7-(-3)\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}7 & 3 \\ 3 & 5.75\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10.093\,75 \\ -2.187\,5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1.75 \\ 0.125\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{31.25}[\begin{aligned}64.093\,75 \\ 17.703\,125\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-0.301 \\ -0.442\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
